extracted.intended_audience: HUD program staff, environmental review officers, grant recipients, state/local implementers, and public commenters on HUD floodplain/wetland policy
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed HUD rule implementing Executive Orders 11988 (Floodplain Management) and 11990 (Protection of Wetlands), specifying applicability, definitions, decisionmaking (an eight-step process), standards (100- and 500-year floodplain), exceptions, documentation, and coordination with FEMA/NEPA/NFIP for HUD programs and grant recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal policy to avoid/adverse impact on wetlands and floodplains (Executive Orders 11988/11990)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Orders 11988 and 11990 establish Federal policy to assure that Federal programs avoid adverse impact on wetlands and floodplains; minimize destruction, loss or degradation of wetlands; preserve and enhance the natural and beneficial values of wetlands; reduce risk of flood loss; minimize the impact of floods on human safety, health, and welfare; and to the extent possible, restore the natural and beneficial values served by floodplains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agencies are required to exercise leadership to assure the intent of the Executive Orders is understood and incorporated whenever possible into Federal, State, or local programs affecting floodplains and wetlands. Under EO 11988 agencies should avoid supporting floodplain development unless there are no practicable alternatives; EO 11990 directs avoidance of Federal assistance for new construction in wetlands unless no practicable alternative exists and measures to minimize harm are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt 100-year base flood standard as minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB and FEMA affirmed the 100-year base flood as the minimum level of protection for Federal actions that develop or improve structures and facilities in floodplains; HUD proposes to conform its standards to the Federal 100-year base flood standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD will revise HUD Minimum Property Standards (24 CFR 200.926d(c)(4)) and related rules to accord with the 100-year base flood standard (and FEMA NFIP regulations, including variance/exception procedures under 44 CFR 60.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: 500-year floodplain standard for 'critical actions'
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types of projects designated as 'critical actions' are covered by the 500-year floodplain standard (proposed § 55.2(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical actions include hospitals, nursing homes, convalescent homes, intermediate care facilities, board and care facilities, and retirement service centers; housing for independent living for the elderly is not a 'critical action'. Housing for elderly that is not a critical action is subject to the 100-year standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eight-step decisionmaking process (§55.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before conducting, supporting, or allowing any action in a floodplain or providing assistance for new construction in a wetland, HUD must (1) determine that the floodplain or wetland site is the only practicable location for such action and (2) if it is the only practicable location, design or modify the action to minimize harm to, or within, the floodplain or wetland where practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §55.20 implements the requirement of the Executive Orders and corresponds to the format in the WRC Guidelines; HUD must conduct an eight-step decisionmaking process (as described in WRC) prior to initial approval of proposed actions in a floodplain or wetland and in conjunction with NEPA (24 CFR part 50) or part 58 reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of key terms and assignment of responsibilities (Subpart A/B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule contains definitions of key terms used in the Executive Orders, WRC Guidelines, and FEMA's NFIP regulations (e.g., 'critical action', 'base flood', 'functionally-dependent use', 'substantial improvement') and assigns responsibilities for functions in implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear definitions are necessary for applicability and for determining which actions must follow the decisionmaking process; §55.11/§55.12 use these definitions to identify covered activities and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability table (§55.11) and excepted HUD program categories (§55.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: §55.11 contains a table indicating compliance requirements by type of HUD program activity and floodplain/wetland location; §55.12 replaces 1979 'categorical exclusions' with 'excepted HUD program categories' that: (i) involve impacts but are protected under NFIP, (ii) do not involve impacts, or (iii) involve de minimis impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table's vertical column groups HUD activities into 'critical actions' and other actions; the horizontal columns refer to four types of floodplain/wetland locations. The table points to §55.20 decisionmaking when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and treatment of 'functionally-dependent uses'
rubrics_metrics.description: Functionally-dependent uses are uses that cannot be conducted to perform their intended purposes unless located in close proximity to water (e.g., marinas, bridges, piers); such uses are reviewed for their effect on floodways (§55.22(b)(4)) or coastal high hazard areas (§55.2(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory provisions for functionally-dependent uses are included to allow their necessary location near water while still addressing floodplain/wetland concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial improvement definition aligned with NFIP (44 CFR 59.1) and HUD density considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule would include a definition of 'substantial improvement' that accords with FEMA's NFIP regulations at 44 CFR 59.1 but also considers density increases in accordance with HUD environmental review procedures at 24 CFR 50.20(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency with NFIP rules ensures alignment for improvements; HUD will set standards for structures with and without basements, coastal high hazard areas, and critical actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of HUD Minimum Property Standards (24 CFR 200.926d(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to 24 CFR 200.926d(c)(4) to conform to the 100-year base flood standard for new construction and substantial improvement of residential structures with basements under NFIP regulations, and to set standards for structures without basements, in coastal high hazard areas, or containing critical actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revision will also incorporate NFIP variance/exception procedures and align HUD mortgage underwriting and minimum grades for buildings/openings to prevent adverse effects by flood levels equivalent to a 100-year return frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linkage with NEPA and HUD environmental review procedures (24 CFR parts 50 and 58)
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD's review of affected proposed actions under 24 CFR part 55 is to be conducted in conjunction with environmental review responsibilities under 24 CFR part 50 (NEPA) and, for grantees, under part 58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with part 55 must be completed before HUD's initial approval of proposed actions in a floodplain or wetland; part 55 designation of categorical exclusions under parts 50 and 58 does not exempt actions from part 55 requirements where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inapplicability/exclusions for certain HUD program activities (rationales)
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD identifies categories of program activities that would not need to comply with Subpart C decisionmaking because compliance would serve no functional purpose: (1) controlled sufficiently under FEMA's NFIP, (2) do not have direct or indirect development impact on floodplains/wetlands, or (3) have de minimis impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: FHA financing decisions for existing one- to four-family properties are proposed to be excluded because there are no practicable locational alternatives, impacts are de minimis, and compliance would serve no functional purpose; such properties in communities in good standing under NFIP remain subject to NFIP hazard minimization for later substantial improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of HUD-acquired properties: documentation and proposed exclusion for 1–4 family
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposition of HUD-acquired properties in 100-year (or 500-year for critical actions) floodplains/wetlands would be subject to documentation and notification requirements in §55.22, but HUD proposes excluding one- to four-family property dispositions from Subpart C because avoidance is impossible (no practicable alternatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion applies only where community is in good standing with NFIP; substantial improvements of those properties must comply with NFIP hazard minimization requirements; HUD seeks comments on this proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedures for notification, conveyance restrictions, and fund availability (§55.21–§55.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 55.21 (notification), 55.22 (conveyance restrictions for disposition of real property), and 55.23 (notification of fund availability) include special procedures to meet Executive Order requirements and HUD concerns for public notice of floodplain or wetland hazards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions address public notice, restrictions on conveyance of real property in floodplains/wetlands, and how HUD notifies about availability of funds where floodplain/wetland hazards are implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation and areawide compliance (§55.24 and §55.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 55.24 and 55.25 provide opportunities for HUD, a local government, or contiguous local governments to minimize duplicative documentation for similar HUD actions in a community-wide or areawide context and to enhance floodplain and wetland planning and management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions encourage coordinated, programmatic compliance to reduce paperwork and improve planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of another agency's review (§55.26) to avoid duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 55.26 would permit HUD or grant recipients to adopt another Federal agency's review under the Executive Orders to minimize regulatory burden and avoid duplication of evaluation efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows leveraging prior Federal analyses (e.g., FEMA reviews) when appropriate, reducing redundant processes for HUD and grantees subject to part 58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum documentation requirements for HUD Field Offices/grant recipients (§55.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 55.27 clarifies the minimum documentation requirements that HUD Field Offices or grant recipients must maintain for compliance under §§55.20, 55.24, 55.25, or 55.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what records and documentation must be kept to demonstrate compliance with the decisionmaking process, areawide or adopted reviews, and to support determinations about practicable alternatives and minimization measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of compliance: complete before initial approval and integrated with decision points
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with part 55 must be completed for applicable activities before the Department's initial approval of proposed actions in a floodplain or wetland, parallel to decision points described in 24 CFR 50.17(a)-(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, the part 55 decisionmaking is performed in conjunction with other environmental review steps so actions are not approved before floodplain/wetland compliance is resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with FEMA/NFIP, CEQ, and WRC Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD's procedures are developed in consultation with FEMA, CEQ, and WRC; FEMA administers NFIP and provides regulatory standards and guidance (including the 100-year base flood), and WRC Guidelines provide the eight-step decisionmaking framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD may rely on FEMA's NFIP regulatory mechanisms to substitute for certain Executive Order requirements and aligns definitions/standards (e.g., 'substantial improvement') with NFIP where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and docket procedures for the proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD sets a comment due date (Comment Due Date: March 5, 1990) and invites interested persons to submit comments to the Rules Docket Clerk at HUD, directing communications to the docket number and title and giving reasons for recommendations. Copies of communications will be available for public inspection at HUD's Rules Docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should state reasons for recommendations; public inspection hours are provided; the rule explains how to send comments and that communications will be available for inspection. (This mirrors standard notice-and-comment procedure.)
